heroSummary: The Bambu Lab X1C handles Sunlu PETG exceptionally well right out of the box using its standard hardened steel direct-drive setup. Running a safe volumetric flow cap of 15 mm³/s yields reliable top speeds up to 179 mm/s without compromising layer adhesion.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with liquid glue or glue stick as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 15 mm³/s in the filament settings to prevent under-extrusion at 179 mm/s.
Lower the Part Cooling Fan to 20% minimum and 50% maximum to ensure high layer bonding strength.
Enable Wipe While Retracting (2 mm distance) and set Retraction Length to 0.8 mm to mitigate PETG oozing and stringing.
Turn off or limit the Auxiliary Part Cooling Fan to 0% to prevent edge curling and warping on larger prints.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG absorbs ambient moisture quickly and has high melt viscosity causing nozzle drool.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament at 65°C for 6 hours, lower nozzle temperature to 235-240°C, and enable Z-hop with retraction wipe.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG chemically fuses directly with clean smooth or textured PEI surfaces during cooling.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a thin, even coat of Bambu Liquid Glue or glue stick to serve as a sacrificial release interface.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling or chamber auxiliary fan chilling the extruded plastic too quickly.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Disable the auxiliary chamber fan completely and cap the main part cooling fan between 30% and 50%.

faq.question: Should the X1C chamber door be open or closed when printing Sunlu PETG?
faq.answer: Keep the glass door closed or slightly vented in warm ambient rooms; PETG benefits from a draft-free environment around 35-40°C to prevent warping.

faq.question: Why does Sunlu PETG rip pieces off my build plate?
faq.answer: PETG forms an extremely strong molecular bond with PEI. Always apply a release agent like glue stick or liquid glue before printing.

faq.question: Can I print Sunlu PETG faster than 179 mm/s on the X1C?
faq.answer: Exceeding 179 mm/s at 0.2mm layer height and 0.42mm line width surpasses the 15 mm³/s melt rate, leading to matte finish, weak layer bonding, and extrusion clicking.

faq.question: Does Sunlu PETG require drying right out of the sealed vacuum bag?
faq.answer: Yes, PETG often retains residual moisture from factory water-bath cooling; drying for 6 hours at 65°C eliminates stringing and micro-bubbles.
